title: The Brunies brothers and George Brunies joining Kelly
summary: Discussing the Brunies family, he recalls George on a doorstep in 1919 and getting offered a job with Bert Kelly, later Ted Lewis.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: The Brunus brothers told me he used to be a good trumpet player. Yeah.
And, uh, now Henny, Henny Brunus was a, uh, Richie Brunus was a good trumpet player.
Yeah, he's still living, doesn't play. No. He's cooked on the boats now.
Still works. I think he's sick, though, right now.
Now, Henny, Henny was a, uh, halibut trombone player. That's what they say.
George Brunus, the younger brother. Yeah, little Georgie. Said that Henny was the greatest in the family. That's right.

Now, here's the funny thing. I played the Orphan in 1919, see? And I'm going out in the Irish Channel to see some folks. And who's sitting across the street on the box step with his big bare feet was this punk, Georgie. Yeah. Used to play alto. You know, the old man had a spasm band. Used to play around the markets on Sunday morning. Henny, Merritt, Richie, Abby and Georgie. And doublehead the uncle. Played bass. And they'd stand on the corner and play stuff, see? So, to make a long story short, He said, hey, Raymond. You were just a car guy. I said, yeah. Come here. I want to talk to you. So, I come in. His mother comes over to her. His mother said, uh, Raymond, uh, Georgia got a wire from, from, uh, from one of my, uh, Bert Kelly. Who is he? I said, Kelly, yeah. He said, yeah. He offers him 75 dollars a week. Does that mean a week? I said, yeah, sure, 75 dollars. Oh, now. But this thing, you weren't 75. He says, yeah. If Kelly heard about him, he wants him, wants to give him 75, he'll give him 75 dollars a week. I said, what, what, what the hell can you play? I used to play a little peck horn, see? Yeah. He's a trombone player. Yeah. So, sure enough, next thing I know is, uh, little Georges in Chicago.
Chicago, yeah. He went up there in about 1921 or so. Yeah.
And next thing you know, uh, another guy, another time, I'll meet him in Atlantic City. He's with Ted Lewis.
Ted Lewis, yeah. He joined Ted Lewis.
